pull.title: expenses: add receipt-backed job expense escrow
pull.body:
## Summary
- separate worker compensation (`price`) from optional `expenseBudget` (0–10,000 PLN)
- fund `price + expenseBudget` through the existing publish-with-payment flow while keeping platform fees on labor only
- lock expense money in a dedicated one-per-job escrow with dedicated wallet ledger types
- let the assigned worker submit immutable receipt-backed claims only while the job is `IN_PROGRESS`
- require the receipt to be the worker's same-job `PARTICIPANTS` attachment and prevent reuse of one receipt across claims
- on normal completion reimburse claimed expenses fee-free and refund unused budget to the requester
- on open cancellation refund the full budget; active mutual cancellation with submitted costs is forced into dispute review
- make admin dispute resolution settle/refund expense escrow consistently with the labor decision
- add Flyway V42, focused tests, documentation and a database-backed runtime smoke covering publication funding, receipt claim and settlement conservation

## Financial invariants
- expense reimbursement never increases the service-fee basis
- cumulative claims cannot exceed the original held expense budget
- terminal expense settlement conserves funds: `reimbursed + refunded = budget`
- wallet mutations use dedicated idempotent operation keys/types
- publish-with-payment requires the complete labor + expense amount before creating the job

## Migration
`V42__job_expense_escrow.sql` adds `jobs.expense_budget`, `job_expense_escrows`, `job_expense_claims`, conservation/state checks and receipt uniqueness.

## Validation
Do not merge until all required checks for the exact latest head are green. Any failure will be fixed on this same branch and rerun.

issue.title: expenses: retain claimed receipt evidence
issue.body:
## Summary
- prevent deletion of attachments that already back a job expense claim
- preserve the encrypted storage object as immutable financial evidence after claim creation
- keep ordinary attachment deletion behavior unchanged for attachments that are not part of an expense audit trail
- add regression coverage proving claimed receipts are neither soft-deleted nor removed from storage
- document receipt-retention semantics in the expense model

## Why
The receipt-backed expense flow merged in #106 made claims immutable, but the attachment delete path did not know whether an attachment had already entered the financial audit trail. A worker could therefore attempt to delete the evidence after creating a claim. This slice closes that lifecycle gap before exposing expense claims more broadly in the web UI.

## Migration
No Flyway migration is required. `job_expense_claims.attachment_id` already records the evidence relationship; deletion is now blocked at the attachment service boundary.

## Validation
Do not merge until all required checks for the exact latest head are green. Any failure will be fixed on this same branch and rerun.

issue.title: web: complete receipt-backed expense claim flow
issue.body:
## Summary
- add frontend API bindings for participant expense summaries and receipt-backed claims
- show the protected expense budget, claimed/reimbursed/refunded totals and immutable claim history to job participants
- let the assigned worker pair an eligible private receipt with an amount while the job is `IN_PROGRESS`
- enforce immediate client-side remaining-budget feedback while keeping backend validation authoritative
- mark claimed receipts as retained financial evidence and stop offering their delete action in the UI
- document the end-to-end browser flow and privacy boundary

## Why
The backend expense escrow introduced in #106 and receipt retention from #107 were production-capable, while #109 only exposed worker receipt upload. A worker still could not submit the actual reimbursement claim through the product UI. This slice closes that commercial gap without widening backend permissions or changing financial settlement semantics.

## Migration
No Flyway migration is required. This consumes the existing V42 expense model and endpoints.

## Validation
Do not merge until all required workflow/check runs for the exact latest head complete successfully. Fix any failures on this branch and rerun before merge.
